subject: koala
reasoning:
I'm planning out a koala model built from primitives, aiming for a realistic sitting pose around 0.7 meters tall with proportions matching a real koala's grey body and rounded features, while sticking to well-documented SDK APIs I can trust without testing.

I'm working through the skeleton structure with hips as root, a spine chain up to the head, and separate joints for ears, arms, and sitting hind legs. For the body I'm sweeping along the spine with a radius profile, then adding spherical primitives for the head with slight scaling for shape, and figuring out how to build the large round ears using flattened cylinder or extrude shapes with a paler inner section.

Now I'm detailing the nose as a scaled dark ellipsoid sphere, small dark eyes with highlights, and considering using a paint function to create the pale chest patch by coloring based on surface normal and position rather than a separate mesh.

For fur texture I'll skip risky card-based tufts and instead apply a grain blend between grey and light tones along the y-axis for a furry look.

For the limbs, I'm planning a chain of joints from shoulder to wrist for each koala arm, hanging slightly forward and down, with enough named points to produce a proper tip joint, then adding digit details to the paws for claws.

Now I'm working through the sitting legs: positioning hips, knees, and ankles with hind legs angled forward-out, placing flattened pale-grey foot spheres so their bottoms rest right at floor level within the allowed sink tolerance. I'm also sketching overall koala proportions—spine path from hips through chest to neck, head position and radius—to get a believable ~0.7m sitting height, and starting to define the body as a sweep along that spine curve.

Setting up spine chain and sweep...

I'm tapering the body radius from wide hips to a narrower neck, then repositioning the hip joint lower so the koala's bottom actually sits on the ground instead of floating.

For the head, I'm sizing a slightly squashed sphere positioned to overlap the neck cleanly, then working out ear placement as small circular outlines extruded sideways from the top corners of the head.

I'm using signed left/right offsets scaled by side to position the ears, then checking the geometry: at x=0.1 the head sphere surface only extends to about 0.066 in y/z, so the 0.055-radius ear disc centered at y=0.08 pokes out past the sphere surface rather than sitting flush, which I need to adjust.

Nudging the ear position outward a bit to x=0.11 and up to 0.09 to fix that overlap. Now I'm placing the nose as a scaled dark sphere near the front-top of the face using local forward/up coordinates so it stays big and koala-like regardless of head bone orientation, then moving on to work out the eye placement.

Positioning small dark spheres as eyes to the sides of the face, considering whether to add tiny white highlights but deciding to skip that detail. Then I'm shifting focus to the overall fur coloring scheme — grey body with a paler cream muzzle and chest patch, building a grain-based fur texture and a paint function that swaps in cream where the chest region criteria are met.

Now I'm planning the arm geometry: defining shoulder, elbow, and wrist joint positions for the left arm hugging the body, using a catmull path with named joints so the wrist becomes the tip for attaching the paw.

Figuring out the hierarchy: adding a root "hips" joint since the spine chain needs an unparented first joint, then mapping spine points to spine1/spine2/neck joints at increasing heights, with the head joint parented to neck and positioned above it. I'm now working out which spine joint the arm chain should parent to.

For the legs, I'm sketching sitting hind-leg geometry — hip, knee, ankle joints forming the thigh/shin path, with a flattened foot sphere whose vertical position I'm tuning so it barely touches the floor within the 2% tolerance. Setting up the leg chain call with hip/knee/ankle joint names, parented to hips, tagged as a leg role.

For the arms, I'm doing similar chain setup with shoulder/elbow/wrist joints, then adding paw spheres pinned to the wrist tip, plus small claw spikes radiating forward from the paw using literal direction vectors to avoid frame ambiguity.

I'm mirroring left/right limbs by looping over a sign value and naming joints with L/R suffixes based on that sign, with hips as the root joint and the spine chain sweeping from wide hips to narrower chest using a tapering radius array. I'm adding cream belly/chest coloring via a paint function keyed on surface normal and position, plus fur grain texture, and detailing the face with cream cheek/muzzle spheres, eyes, and highlights positioned relative to the head joint. For the ears, I'm writing a disc-point helper function and extruding outer grey and inner pale ear shapes offset slightly outward along the side axis, checking the extrusion thickness stays within bounds. I'm finalizing leg and arm path coordinates, sweep radii tapering from thigh to ankle and shoulder to wrist, and placing foot/paw spheres with claws, then defining the head joint position and a head sphere parented to the neck, double-checking how the `bone` and `at` options interact for part placement.
